name: Treaty with the Potawatomi, March 29, 1836 (Wau-ke-wa's band)
aka: Treaty on Tippecanoe River with Wau-ke-wa, Che-cose's only son
promises: Article 1: the band ceded the four sections reserved for it by the second article of an earlier Potawatomi treaty.
Article 2: the band would give up possession within three months and remove west of the Mississippi within two years.
Article 3: the United States would pay the band $2,560 in specie at the first annuity payment after ratification.
Article 4: the United States would pay the expenses of making the treaty.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or government finding about this cession was found. The Potawatomi Indiana land cases in Docket 128 et al. that were opened do not mention these four sections.

openQuestions: treaties.json merges two bands (Wau-ke-wa's and Aub-ba-naub-ba's) and two Royce areas (208, 209). DigiTreaties links area 208 to this treaty and area 209 to the April 11, 1836 treaty with Aub-ba-naub-ba's band, which has its own Kappler page. The Aub-ba-naub-ba band may belong on a separate record.
Whether the Indian Claims Commission valued the 1836 band reserve cessions was not found; a pass through the Potawatomi of Indiana and Michigan dockets (29-K and related) is needed.

The Forest County Potawatomi list this treaty among their treaties but give no account of it. Which present-day nations descend from Wau-ke-wa's band was not confirmed; treaties.json names the Citizen Potawatomi Nation.

plain.promised: Wau-ke-wa's band would be paid $2,560 for four reserved sections on the Tippecanoe River in Indiana and would move west within two years.
plain.happened: No court, claims commission or government finding about this cession was found.
plain.today: Nothing was found on whether the price was later reviewed.
